text: Now, for the arahant, the whole world appears like a chessboard.

say: Now, for the arahant, the whole world appears like a chessboard.

text:
It is as if the unending game of chess with all its vicissitudes has
ended in a peaceful draw.

say: It is as if the unending game of chess with all its vicissitudes has ended in a peaceful draw.

text:
Let a myriad arahant lotuses, unsmeared by water and mud, bright
petalled and sweet scented, bloom all over the forest hermitage pond.

say: Let a myriad arahant lotuses, unsmeared by water and mud, bright petalled and sweet scented, bloom all over the forest hermitage pond.

text:
Unravelling the tangled knot of grasping, they form no desire
anywhere in the world.

say: Unravelling the tangled knot of holding on, they form no desire anywhere in the world.

text: He who, having known both ends, with wisdom does not get attached to the middle, him I call a great man, he has gone beyond the seamstress in this world.

say: He who, having known both ends, with wisdom does not get attached to the middle, him I call a great man, he has gone beyond the seamstress in this world.

text:
Are released in the experience of cessation, it is they that are the
dispellers of death.

say: Are released in the experience of stopping, it is they that are the dispellers of death.

text:
It could indeed be expected of a noble disciple who has faith that he
will dwell with energy... that he will be mindful... that he will gain
concentration, will gain one-pointedness of mind, having made release
the object... that he will understand thus: 'This saṃsāra is without a
conceivable beginning... But the remainderless fading away and
cessation of ignorance... the stilling of all preparations... the
destruction of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.' That
wisdom of his, Venerable Sir, is his faculty of wisdom.

say: It could indeed be expected of a noble disciple who has faith that he will dwell with energy... that he will be mindful... that he will gain concentration, will gain one-pointedness of mind, having made release the object... that he will understand thus — 'This samsara is without a conceivable beginning... But the remainderless going out and stopping of not seeing how it works... everything the mind makes comes to a stop... the wanting ends, nothing pulls you any more, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel.' That wisdom of his, Venerable Sir, is his faculty of wisdom.

text:
Whatever is prepared is not worthwhile, and yet, it is by means of
this prepared noble eightfold path that the Buddha clears the path to
the unprepared.

say: Whatever is prepared is not worthwhile, and yet, it is by means of this prepared noble eightfold path that the Buddha clears the path to the unprepared.

text:
The arahant has no such distinction [between this shore and the
farther shore]. Once gone beyond, the emancipated one has no more use
of these concepts.

say: The arahant has no such distinction [between this shore and the farther shore]. Once gone beyond, the emancipated one has no more use of these concepts.

text:
All those who came out of that hall, except this discerning one, were
spectators. He was not one of the audience, because he had an insight
into the magic show from his hiding place on the stage.

say: All those who came out of that hall, except this discerning one, were spectators. He was not one of the audience, because he had an insight into the magic show from his hiding place on the stage.

text:
He knows that, given ignorance, they are true, and that they are
falsified only when ignorance fades away in one who sees the cessation.
Fortified with that understanding, he does not categorically assert the
sense-data as true, nor does he reprimand those who assert them as the
truth. That is why the Buddha advocates a tolerant attitude in this
discourse.

say: He knows that, given not seeing how it works, they are true, and that they are falsified only when not seeing how it works fades away in one who sees the stopping. Fortified with that understanding, he does not categorically assert the sense-data as true, nor does he reprimand those who assert them as the truth. That is why the Buddha advocates a tolerant attitude in this discourse.

text:
To one detached from percepts there are no bonds, to one released
through wisdom there are no delusions, those who hold on to percepts
and views, go about wrangling in this world.

say: To one detached from percepts there are no bonds, to one released through wisdom there are no delusions, those who hold on to percepts and views, go about wrangling in this world.
